correctness.rationale: In a two-sided stationary Poisson construction, the elapsed interval and earlier inter-reset intervals are iid exponentials; independent Brownian increments over them are iid Laplace with scale ℓ=√(D/r). Successive contractions give the stated weighted sum. Its variances are summable and identical-noise coupling contracts any initial difference by a raised to the number of resets, giving uniqueness. Writing w=ℓ²θ², the log product is ∑_{k≥1}w^k/[k(1−e^{−2εk})]; expanding the reciprocal as (2εk)⁻¹+1/2+O(εk), with the error bound valid also for large εk, gives Λ/ε−(1/2)log(1−w)+O(ε) with interior derivatives. At θ_y the tilted mean differs from y/ε by O(1). The tilted Laplace factors after centering and √ε scaling have product modulus bounded by (1+cεt²)^−⌊1/ε⌋, c=ℓ²e⁻². On |t|≤ε⁻¹/² this is bounded by an integrable Gaussian; outside, its integral is bounded by ε⁻¹/²(1+c)^−(⌊1/ε⌋−1) times the integral of (1+cu²)^−1. The characteristic-function limit thus gives uniform density convergence. Integrating the tilted density against e^−θ_y u for overshoot u≥0 gives √ε/[θ_y√(2πΛ″)], and exponentiating the order-one cumulant gives the stated boundary multiplier. For the full LDP, Λ is strictly convex and steep, local lower bounds follow by interior tilts and concentration, and Markov bounds and exponential tightness give the full upper bound. Near zero the quartic cumulant gives the stated negative quartic correction. At large y, 1−(ℓθ_y)²=e^−θ_y y gives y(1/ℓ−θ_y)→0 and Λ→π²/12, proving the claimed intercept.
residual_risks: Relative asymptotic for fixed finite y>0 and fixed ℓ>0, not a crossover uniform in y or a fixed-contraction spatial tail.

evidence: With w=ℓ²z² and q=e^−2ε the stationary MGF is (w;q)_∞⁻¹. The published product asymptotic supplies η(z)=Li₂(ℓ²z²)/2 and ψ(z)=(1−ℓ²z²)^−1/2.

The log-product expansion is locally uniform on |Re z|<1/ℓ by the same trapezoidal estimate: 1−ℓ²z²e^−2u has positive real part and the u derivatives decay integrably uniformly on strip-compacts. The real limiting law is nonlattice and infinitely divisible: for every s>0 exp(sεK_ε(it)) is a characteristic function (each Laplace factor raised to a positive real power is a bilateral gamma characteristic function), and tends to the continuous exp(sη(it)); |exp(η(it))|<1 for nonzero real t by the strictly negative integral of log(1+ℓ²t²e^−2u) with a minus sign.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Apply Thm. 4.3 along any ε_n↓0 with t_n=1/ε_n, X_n=X_{ε_n}, x=y, h=θ_y, F=I_ℓ. Since η′(0)=0 and η′ tends to infinity at the right endpoint, every fixed y>0 qualifies. The theorem yields the frozen formula in full including its endpoint factor, and symmetry yields the left tail. The checks of the strip and reference law use elementary properties of the already published product and require no new sharp-deviation theorem or model-specific estimate beyond the product asymptotic.
